candidates.name: blackmarblepy
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package that pulls NASA Black Marble VNP46 nighttime-lights tiles (daily/monthly/yearly, global, any user-defined date range and region-of-interest polygon) via the NASA LAADS DAAC API, converts HDF5 to georeferenced rasters, mosaics them, and computes zonal statistics/time series. No data committed to the repo itself — pure acquisition + processing tool, free NASA Earthdata token required, no paid key.
candidates.why_useful: Could be pointed at specific Airbnb-heavy tourism geographies (e.g. Cancun, Bali, Algarve, Gold Coast) to build a custom nightlights-based destination-activity index as an occupancy/demand proxy for gap #2 (realised occupancy) or gap #7 (regional travel volume, LatAm/APAC) where no other free series exists. World Bank-maintained, MIT licence, actively updated (last push 7 Sep 2026).

candidates.name: blackmarbler
candidates.what_it_holds: R equivalent of blackmarblepy — same NASA Black Marble VNP46 nighttime-lights download/raster/zonal-stats pipeline, no committed data.
candidates.why_useful: Same use case as blackmarblepy for teams working in R; redundant capability, listed for completeness.

candidates.name: india-district-nightlights-viirs
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed derived-statistics panel at output/csv/nightlights_district_panel.csv: 641 Indian districts x 13 years (2012-2024) = 8,333 rows, with mean/median/sum radiance, std dev, min/max, valid-pixel counts, and log-transformed variants per district-year; also year-wise GeoJSON with district polygons. Raw VIIRS rasters are gitignored (must be re-pulled via Google Earth Engine), but the derived panel itself is committed.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made district-level economic-activity proxy for India, one of ABNB's under-covered APAC growth markets (gap #7, regional travel volume outside US/EU) — could be aggregated to tourism-heavy districts (Goa, Kerala backwaters, Rajasthan) as an occupancy/demand proxy where no official monthly tourism series exists.

candidates.name: chile-night-lights-change
candidates.what_it_holds: VIIRS Black Marble (VNP46A3) nighttime-lights change analysis for Chile across 2014, 2019, 2024: annual composites, deltas, and regional (region-level) metrics. Repo description implies committed regional summary outputs, not just a notebook, but file listing was not independently confirmed.
candidates.why_useful: Chile is one of the LatAm markets named in gap #7 (regional travel volume outside US/EU: LatAm — Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Argentina, and by extension Chile). A regional nightlights delta series could proxy destination-level tourism recovery/growth where DATATUR/INEGI-style official series don't exist for Chile specifically.

candidates.name: light_tiles
candidates.what_it_holds: Per repo description: "All of the light pollution data from the 2025 Earth Observations Group VIIRS Nighttime Lights Study" stored in JSON, described as being for "easy Web Access" — implying a global tile-based mirror of the EOG VNL product converted to JSON. Could not confirm file listing or exact size (README fetch 404'd on both main and master branches at time of scouting; needs a directory-listing check before relying on it).
candidates.why_useful: If genuine, a committed global nightlights dataset (not just an API client) would remove the NASA Earthdata token / API-pull step needed by blackmarblepy/blackmarbler above, making a global tourism-destination nightlights index buildable offline. Flagged for a follow-up directory-listing check (gh api repos/AndrewMulert/light_tiles/contents) rather than confirmed.

candidates.name: nighttime-radiance
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scripts and Jupyter notebooks to download and preprocess VIIRS DNB (Day/Night Band) nighttime-lights data from NOAA/NASA sources; no data committed, method/pipeline only.
candidates.why_useful: Lighter-weight alternative to blackmarblepy for a one-off pull of VIIRS DNB imagery over a specific tourism destination bounding box; BSD-3 licensed.

candidates.name: NighttimeLights.jl
candidates.what_it_holds: Julia package to analyse VIIRS nighttime-lights data (processing/statistics functions); no committed geography-specific dataset.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose analysis tool if the team ever works in Julia; not tourism-specific.

candidates.name: syria-economic-monitor (and sibling datapartnership/*-economic-monitor repos)
candidates.what_it_holds: World Bank Data Partnership template repo combining remote sensing (nighttime lights, port/trade activity via satellite), mobility patterns, internet connectivity, and vegetation conditions to track economic activity in data-scarce countries. Same org has near-identical repos for Niger, Algeria, Egypt, Ethiopia, Myanmar, Morocco — a reusable methodology, not Airbnb-market data itself (all current instances cover conflict/data-scarce non-ABNB markets).
candidates.why_useful: Not directly usable (wrong geographies) but is a concrete, working template for combining nightlights + mobility + connectivity into a single "economic activity monitor" — the same recipe could be forked and re-pointed at an ABNB-relevant tourism destination (e.g. a LatAm or APAC market from gap #7) faster than building from scratch.
candidates.geography: Syria, Niger, Algeria, Egypt, Ethiopia, Myanmar, Morocco (none are core ABNB markets)
candidates.time_coverage: varies by country monitor, generally recent (2023-2026)
candidates.size_hint: notebooks + processed indicator files per country repo

notes: This theme returned almost nothing tourism-specific on GitHub: no repos surfaced for 'parking lot satellite count', 'Sentinel-2 tourism', 'satellite occupancy hotel', or 'nightlights tourism' as literal phrases (all returned zero results via gh search repos). What exists in volume is generic VIIRS/Black Marble nighttime-lights tooling and country-level GDP/conflict/urban-growth studies (World Bank Data Partnership country monitors, university GIS class projects) with no tourism or short-term-rental framing at all — this looks like a genuine gap in the open-source ecosystem rather than a search-term problem: nightlights-for-tourism and satellite-parking-lot-counts are done commercially (RS Metrics, Orbital Insight, SpaceKnow) but not open-sourced on GitHub. The closest usable things are general-purpose NASA Black Marble access libraries (blackmarblepy/blackmarbler, World Bank-maintained) that a team could point at specific destination bounding boxes to build its own proxy from scratch, plus one committed India district-level derived panel. Caveat on methodology: gh search repos returned literal zero-result arrays for several exact-phrase queries, which may undercount recall (GitHub's search API is not always phrase-tolerant) — a code-search pass (not available under this scout's tool budget) or a differently-phrased query set might surface more. Also note: mid-session, the shared WebSearch budget for this run was already exhausted (200/200) before this scout could use it, and GitHub's own web search UI returned HTTP 429 on WebFetch — both external-search fallbacks were unavailable, so this scout is likely under-covering compared to scouts that ran earlier in the sweep. Recommend a follow-up scout re-run this theme once search budgets reset, and also try 'nightlight tourism econometrics' style academic-paper searches (Google Scholar / Zenodo) since the academic literature on using VIIRS for tourism monitoring (e.g. Sicily, Balearic Islands studies) exists but its replication code was not found committed to GitHub in this pass.
